overview:
**Extreme fire danger continues across the Montrose High Elevation area today, driven by critically dry fuels (98% ERC) and single-digit humidity.**
- Danger holds at Extreme through Monday, then eases to Very High Tuesday–Wednesday and High by next weekend as afternoon humidity slowly recovers.
- Northeast winds near 8 mph and a high near 92°F will keep afternoons hot, with patchy morning smoke clearing by midday.
- 4 of 7 local watchout thresholds are exceeded (ERC, BI, min/max RH) — WATCHOUT conditions in effect; no Red Flag Warning is posted today, but NWS Grand Junction Air Quality Alerts remain active for wildfire smoke.
- Gunnison County has been in Stage 2 Fire Restrictions since June 30, and Ouray County implemented Stage 2 restrictions for unincorporated areas effective June 28, 2026; Montrose County remains under Stage 1 restrictions on BLM lands.
- Nearby fires: Gold Mountain Fire near Ouray is 39,507 acres, 90% contained; Elk Fire in the Gunnison National Forest is 5,117 acres, 40% contained.
